stem: A technician photographs one upper flower and reports the crop is ready because that sample contains many amber glandular trichomes. What is the strongest next step?
choices: Use the upper-flower image as the crop estimate because top-canopy tissue is the most exposed and therefore the most informative sample
Collect repeated observations from comparable floral tissues across representative canopy positions before deciding maturity
Use the cultivar's expected flowering duration as the primary decision and consult trichomes only when the calendar is unclear
Use the first clearly amber sample as the harvest trigger because visible amber development provides a consistent crop-wide threshold
rationale: Maturation can vary among tissues, canopy positions, plant ages, and genotypes. Repeated representative observations provide stronger evidence than one extreme sample.
